services.name: IUI treatment
services.summary: IUI is a gentle, less invasive first step for many couples. We time the procedure carefully with your natural cycle to give you the best possible chance of conception.

children.text: Service overview

Our IUI programme offers a gentle, well-timed first step for couples and individuals trying to conceive. We combine careful cycle tracking, prepared sperm samples and close follow-up to give you the best possible chance.
We provide care for conditions
Unexplained infertility
Mild male factor infertility
Ovulation disorders such as PCOS
Cervical mucus or cervical factor issues
Single women and same-sex couples using donor sperm

services.cardsHeading: Gentle fertility care, step by step

children.text: How much does IUI treatment cost?
The cost depends on whether medication, extra scans or donor sperm are needed. We share a clear, itemised estimate before you start, so you can plan each cycle with confidence.
What to expect during your IUI cycle
We review your history, run baseline tests and agree a plan that suits your cycle.
Scans track your follicles, and the insemination is timed to your ovulation for the best chance of success.
About two weeks later you take a pregnancy test, and we talk through the result and next steps together.
Conclusion
IUI is a simple, low-stress option for many people starting their fertility journey. With careful timing and steady support, our team helps you move forward with clarity.

services.quote: “They made our first IUI cycle feel calm and simple from start to finish.”

children.text: How much does IVF treatment cost?

What to expect during your IVF journey

The best embryo is transferred, and we support you closely until your first pregnancy scan.
Conclusion
IVF can feel like a big step, but you never take it alone. With one dedicated specialist and a caring team, we help you move through every stage with confidence.

children.text: Service overview
Egg freezing gives you more choice about when to start a family. Our specialists guide you through stimulation, retrieval and secure long-term storage with careful monitoring and honest advice.
We provide care for conditions
Planning to delay pregnancy for personal or career reasons
Upcoming cancer treatment that may affect fertility
Low or declining ovarian reserve
Endometriosis or ovarian surgery
Family history of early menopause
How much does egg freezing cost?
The total cost depends on medication, the number of cycles you need and how long eggs are stored. We explain every part of the price upfront so you can plan with confidence.
What to expect when freezing your eggs
We start with a consultation and fertility tests to see how many eggs you are likely to collect.
About two weeks of medication and monitoring prepare your eggs before a short retrieval procedure.
Mature eggs are frozen and stored safely until you decide to use them in the future.
Conclusion
Egg freezing is a practical way to protect future options. With clear advice and attentive care, we help you make the decision that is right for you.

articles.title: Hydration Tips for Fertility Care and Pregnancy
articles.summary: Simple hydration habits that support your energy, hormones and overall wellbeing during fertility care and pregnancy.

children.text: Intro
Water supports almost every system your body relies on during fertility treatment and pregnancy, from hormone balance to healthy circulation.
Signs you need more water
Feeling tired or light-headed during the day.
Dark yellow urine or headaches.
Dry lips, skin or eyes.
Constipation, especially in pregnancy.
Why hydration matters
Even mild dehydration can leave you tired and affect how your body responds to medication.
During pregnancy, your blood volume increases, so your body needs more fluid than usual.
“Hydration is one of the simplest habits with some of the biggest everyday benefits.”
How much is enough?
Most women need around eight to ten glasses a day, more in hot weather or after exercise.
Your needs may change during treatment, so ask your specialist what is right for you.
Easy ways to drink more
Keep a refillable bottle with you.
Add fruit slices for natural flavour.
Eat water-rich foods like cucumber, watermelon and soups.
Conclusion
Small, steady hydration habits support your energy and wellbeing at every stage of your journey.

articles.title: Your First Fertility Appointment: What to Expect
articles.summary: A calm, step-by-step guide to your first fertility appointment, from what to bring to the questions worth asking.

children.text: Intro
Your first fertility consultation is about understanding your story. There is no pressure to decide anything on the day.
What to bring
Any previous test results or scan reports.
Dates of your last few menstrual cycles.
A list of current medications and supplements.
Your questions, written down so nothing is forgotten.
What happens during the visit
Your specialist will ask about your health, cycle, lifestyle and how long you have been trying to conceive.
We will explain which tests may help and why, so you understand every step before it happens.
“A good first consultation should leave you with clarity, not more questions.”
Common first tests
Most couples start with hormone blood tests, a pelvic ultrasound and a semen analysis.
These simple tests give us a clear picture and help us recommend the right next step.
Questions worth asking
What could be affecting our chances?
Which tests do you recommend first, and why?
What are our treatment options and timelines?
Conclusion
Coming prepared helps you get the most from your visit, and our team will guide you through every next step with care.

articles.title: Simple Daily Self-Care Rituals for Pregnancy
articles.summary: Easy daily self-care ideas that help you rest, move and feel more like yourself throughout pregnancy.

children.text: Intro
Pregnancy changes your body and your routines. Small daily rituals can help you rest, stay connected to yourself and feel more at ease.
Everyday self-care ideas
A short walk in daylight to lift your mood and energy.
Ten minutes of stretching or prenatal yoga before bed.
A warm (not hot) bath to ease tired muscles.
Writing down three things you are looking forward to.
Rest is part of the plan
Fatigue is common, especially in the first and third trimesters. Short rests through the day are not a luxury, they are part of a healthy pregnancy.
Try to keep a regular sleep routine and use pillows to support your back and bump.
“Looking after yourself is one of the first ways you look after your baby.”
Caring for your emotional health
Mood changes are normal, but persistent low mood or anxiety deserve attention. Talking to someone early makes a real difference.
Stay connected with friends and family, and let people help with meals or chores.
Before trying something new
Check new exercise with your doctor or midwife.
Avoid saunas, hot tubs and very hot baths.
Choose pregnancy-safe skincare and massage oils.
Conclusion
Self-care in pregnancy does not need to be complicated. Simple, consistent habits help you feel more like yourself every day.

articles.title: IVF vs IUI: Which Fertility Treatment Is Right for You
articles.summary: A clear comparison of IVF and IUI, how each treatment works and who each one is best suited for.

children.text: Intro
IVF and IUI are two of the most common fertility treatments. They work in different ways, and the right choice depends on your age, history and test results.
IUI at a glance
Prepared sperm is placed directly in the uterus around ovulation.
Less invasive and usually less costly than IVF.
Often recommended as a first step for unexplained infertility.
May be combined with gentle medication to support ovulation.
How IVF works
IVF begins with medication to help several eggs mature. The eggs are collected, fertilised in our lab, and the healthiest embryo is transferred to the uterus.
Because fertilisation happens in the lab, IVF can help when tubes are blocked, sperm counts are low or other treatments have not worked.
“There is no single best treatment. The best option is the one that fits your body, your timeline and your goals.”
Success rates and timelines
IVF generally has higher success rates per cycle, while IUI is simpler and can be repeated over several months.
Your specialist will explain realistic expectations based on your own results, not general averages.
How we help you decide
Review your history and any previous treatment.
Complete hormone, ultrasound and semen tests.
Talk through options, costs and timelines together.
Conclusion
Whichever path you choose, you will have a dedicated team guiding you through every step, from the first scan to the result.

articles.title: Fertility Diet: Key Nutrients During Treatment
articles.summary: Practical food choices and key nutrients that help your body feel prepared during fertility treatment.

children.text: Intro
What you eat cannot guarantee a pregnancy, but a balanced diet gives your body the best possible foundation during fertility treatment.
Building a fertility-friendly plate
Half your plate as colourful vegetables and fruit.
Whole grains such as oats, brown rice and wholemeal bread.
Lean proteins including fish, eggs, beans and lentils.
Healthy fats from olive oil, nuts, seeds and avocado.
Nutrients worth focusing on
Folate supports early development, which is why most women trying to conceive are advised to take a daily supplement.
Iron, vitamin D and omega-3 fats also play important roles. A simple blood test can show whether you need extra support.
“Small, steady changes to your daily meals are far more sustainable than a strict diet you cannot keep up.”
Foods to limit
Keep caffeine moderate, avoid alcohol and limit highly processed foods that are high in sugar and salt.
Partners matter too. Healthy eating supports sperm quality, so it helps to make these changes together.
Simple habits to start this week
Plan three balanced meals before you shop.
Keep a bottle of water with you through the day.
Swap one sugary snack for fruit or a handful of nuts.
Conclusion
Good nutrition is one part of a bigger picture. Our specialists can tailor advice to your treatment plan and your health history.

articles.title: Your Third Trimester Checklist for a Calm Birth
articles.summary: What to plan, pack and prioritise in the last months of pregnancy so you feel calm and ready.

children.text: Intro
The third trimester is the home stretch. Your body is working hard, and a little planning now helps the last weeks feel calmer and more in your control.
What to prepare in advance
Pack your hospital bag by week 35, including documents, comfortable clothes and baby essentials.
Agree a simple birth plan with your care team and share it with your partner.
Arrange help at home for the first two weeks after birth.
Save your clinic and labour ward numbers somewhere easy to find.
Why the last weeks matter
Your baby gains most of their weight in these final months, and regular check-ups let us track growth, position and your blood pressure closely.
This is also the time to talk openly about how you feel. Tiredness and worry are common, and your specialist can help with both.
“Preparing early is not about controlling every detail. It is about giving yourself space to rest when the time comes.”
Looking after your body
Gentle walks, pelvic floor exercises and good sleep support your body as it gets ready for labour.
Eat little and often, stay hydrated and tell us straight away about swelling, headaches or reduced movements.
Questions to ask at your next visit
What signs mean I should come in straight away?
How will we decide if induction is needed?
What pain relief options are available to me?
Conclusion
With a clear plan, the right support and regular check-ups, you can approach your due date feeling prepared and confident.
